featuresTitle: The details you need. When you need them.

features.title: Live ride data
features.body: Speed, battery, power, temperature, and PWM headroom at a glance, with readings from your PEV.

features.title: Your ride history

guide.compatibilityTitle: Does it work with your PEV?
guide.compatibilityBody: CutOut is intended for VESC Onewheel + Refloat, EUC, eskate, scooter, ebike and emoto. The developer owns the first two categories; the others need community data captures. Manufacturer-encrypted communications are not supported.

A little help

questions.title: Which PEV types is CutOut for?
questions.body: CutOut is intended for VESC-powered Onewheels running Refloat, EUCs, eskates, scooters, ebikes and emotos. The developer owns VESC Onewheel + Refloat and EUC hardware. Eskate, scooter, ebike and emoto support needs community captures. Individual model and firmware capabilities still need implementation and validation.

questions.title: Will you support devices with encrypted communications?
questions.body: No. CutOut will not support devices whose manufacturers encrypt their communications. Unencrypted devices from the same manufacturer can be considered independently.

questions.title: How can I help add support for my PEV?
questions.body: Community data captures are needed for eskates, scooters, ebikes and emotos. Contact the project with the device model and firmware to ask for capture instructions. Do not post private captures in a public GitHub issue; recordings can contain device identifiers and location.

questions.title: Does a stock Onewheel work?
questions.body: The Onewheel scope here is a VESC-powered build running Refloat. This does not claim support for stock Onewheel electronics or manufacturer-encrypted protocols.

questions.title: Which Bluetooth RGB lights work?
questions.body: MELK devices are supported now, with more planned. Our goal is to support all non-encrypted Bluetooth RGB devices. Choose colors, white, brightness and supported effects, and save named presets. Available effects depend on the controller and firmware.

questions.title: Which Wi-Fi cameras work with CutOut?
questions.body: The current camera profile is FreedConn R3 Pro with R3V1 firmware. It supports live preview and camera media access, with recording and still-photo controls when the firmware offers them. Other models and firmware need validation; a Novatek processor alone does not establish compatibility.

questions.title: Which other Wi-Fi cameras are being researched?
questions.body: These action, body and bicycle/motorcycle cameras are compatibility candidates, not confirmed CutOut support. Some have published research on a related Novatek control protocol; others have only confirmed Novatek hardware and Wi-Fi. Exact firmware and camera functions still need testing. Vehicle-mounted systems may need external power.

questions.title: Why is CutOut open source?
questions.body: The primary goal is to make it easier to build better apps for all PEVs. We share the protocol work and libraries so other developers can focus on their own ideas. We also want a CutOut app its creator likes and the community wants to use. Building a very good app helps make those shared libraries useful.

questions.title: Can I build my own app with the libraries?
questions.body: Yes. All CutOut code is open source today, including reusable Rust libraries and mobile bindings. The project is in alpha: APIs can change, and source availability does not mean every device or feature is ready. Start with the source and examples.

questions.title: Are Bluetooth diagnostics sent automatically?
questions.body: No. Bluetooth capture is a separate, manually started diagnostic workflow. You choose whether to share a capture. Captures can contain device identifiers and location, so keep private files out of public reports.

questions.title: Where are my rides stored?
questions.body: Your saved rides are stored on your phone. Open your ride history to browse routes and recorded details.

questions.title: Can I see what I was listening to on a ride?
questions.body: Yes. Turn on listening history to save the songs you listen to during a ride. CutOut saves song details with your ride, not audio.

questions.title: Can I record a ride without connecting a PEV?
questions.body: Yes. Start a GPS-only ride to record your route without a connected device. Device readings are available when a supported PEV is connected.

questions.title: Are charging spots guaranteed to be available?
questions.body: Charging spots and access notes come from the community. Read the details, check that the plug works with your charger, and confirm access with the location when needed.

questions.title: What happens when I delete my community account?
questions.body: Your account-linked private records are deleted. Public charging spots remain under Anonymous with their content unchanged; you can remove your spots manually first if you wish. Local rides and Bluetooth captures remain on your device. The privacy policy explains deletion receipts and backup retention.

soundtrack.title: What was your soundtrack?
soundtrack.body: Keep track of what you were listening to on each ride. Rediscover the songs that went with a favorite route.

accessories.title: Make it your kind of bright.
accessories.body: Choose your colors, set the brightness and find an effect that fits your setup. Save your favorite looks as presets, ready for the next ride.

accessories.title: Your ride camera. Right here.
accessories.body: Preview a supported Wi-Fi camera, start and stop recording, or take a photo from CutOut. Browse the camera’s footage and download the clips you want to keep.

openSource.title: Good ideas are worth sharing.
openSource.body: All CutOut code is open source. The libraries behind the app give other PEV developers a place to start, with the protocol work already underway.

about.title:
A better ride.
More room for ideas.
about.body: CutOut is a ride app built by a rider, with the PEV community. All the code is open source, and the project is in alpha.

sections.title: Better PEV apps.
sections.body: The primary goal is to make it easier for everyone to build better PEV apps. Share the protocol work and useful libraries so the next developer can spend more time on their own ideas.

sections.title: An app worth riding with.
sections.body: The next goal is to build a CutOut app its creator likes and the community wants to use. The best way to get there is to build a very good app. Real rides and real devices also make the shared libraries better.

sections.title: Build on what is here.
sections.body: Use the Rust libraries for device and accessory protocols, ride data, maps, music metadata and persistence, with mobile bindings for app integration. The APIs are alpha and still changing.
